cues: Paired connectives come in two halves, and both must be present.
Both and, with a plural verb.
Neither nor, never neither or, and the verb follows the nearer subject.
Not only but also, with the same grammatical shape on both sides.
So with an adjective, such with a noun: so tired that, such a cold night that.
And two pairs that are already negative, so never add not: the box is too heavy to lift; work hard lest you should fail.

Not only but also, with the same grammatical shape on both sides. Whether or not. So with an adjective, such with a noun: so tired that, such a cold night that. And two pairs that are already negative, so never add not: the box is too heavy to lift; work hard lest you should fail.
